title: Δ4 act-class subject taxonomy (family contract §4 Δ4; DESIGN.md §13.2; delivered in C2)
description: The closed BPA-1-expressible subject taxonomy Δ4 delivers in C2: the five act classes model_egress | share | outbound | apply | budget (family contract §4, verbatim) are the whole governed-act vocabulary, carried in ActIntent subjects and bounded by Mandates/StandingMandateRevisions; the gate inbox renders pending prepared intents and eligible seats (L48–L50). subject_atoms is EXACTLY the BPA-1 request-atoms wire (spec/schemas/bpa1-policy.schema.json requestAtoms): one concrete value per supplied domain, compiled by the kernel from the dependency closure (§10.6), never caller-shaped — the copied $defs here are byte-identical to bpa1-policy's and the conformance runner machine-checks both that equality and, per vector, that every subject decides through the BPA-1 reference evaluator policy/eval.py (the taxonomy↔BPA-1 cross-validation). Each class arm pins its mandatory domains (this pinning is itself the C2 deliverable — Δ4 defines no other source); extra domains only narrow further and are always allowed. An allow rule requires a constrained domain present and matching; a deny rule conservatively matches an absent domain — so a subject omitting a non-mandatory domain fails closed against policies constraining it.

act_class.description: Family contract Δ4 verbatim: the closed act-class list.

oneOf.$comment: A model call leaving through the broker: the exact provider binding, the classification of what is disclosed, and a quantity ceiling (token/output-byte dimension) are mandatory.
Disclosure of an exact object to another party or scope: the object and its classification are mandatory.
Bytes leaving to a network peer (Akson dispatch, webhook): the exact network destination and classification are mandatory.
Digest-bound workspace apply (family contract L60): the exact object, path, and offered schema/evidence digest tuple are mandatory — the driver refuses a moved target or stale fence.
A budget change or spend act: the exact quantity (dimension, unit, scale, amount) is mandatory.

aLabelHost.description: Lowercase A-label (punycode) hostname, LDH labels of at most 63 octets (§10.5: A-label hostname; no free text, no wildcard).

atomPurpose.description: §10.5 purpose row: 'Exact purpose ref or descendant in a pinned acyclic purpose snapshot.' snapshot pins the exact acyclic purpose snapshot (typed DigestRef); path is the materialized root-to-node ancestor chain from that snapshot (verified against the pin at preparation), so descendant testing is pure path-prefix comparison — no resolution inside the algebra. The atom covers the named node and its descendants; atoms over different snapshots are incomparable (typed reject).

atomRate.description: §10.5 rate row: 'Exact integer token-bucket RateCeiling and authority-server epoch; subset uses capacity/refill/burst containment.' Fields verbatim from the §10.5 RateCeiling record (integer discrete refill; clock is always authority_server). Atoms differing in dimension, canonical_unit, or epoch are incomparable (typed reject). Subset is the §10.5 containment: capacity <= capacity, max_burst <= max_burst, and refill-rate containment by exact integer cross-multiplication (child.refill_amount * parent.refill_period_milliseconds <= parent.refill_amount * child.refill_period_milliseconds — no floats). Worst-case boundary-alignment dominance beyond this containment is enforced at consume time by atomic ancestor-counter locking (§10.5) — ADR-0001 open item.

atomSchemaEvidence.description: §10.5 schema/evidence row: 'Exact immutable schema, verifier, attestor, and assurance-policy digests.' One exact digest tuple per atom (alternatives are separate rules); subset and intersection are exact tuple equality.

currencyCode.description: ISO 4217 alphabetic currency code (§10.5 money quantities name ISO currency).

digestRef.$comment: The closed family DigestRef wire (family-vectors/PROFILE.md §6.1, normative; D-R0-1): exactly the members {class, algorithm, key_ref?, value_hex}. The oneOf pins the closed class/algorithm pairing and requires key_ref exactly for the keyed erasure classes; each arm refines members of this already-closed object.

class.description: Digest class (PROFILE.md §6, D-R0-1); substituting one class where a schema requires another is a conformance failure.

key_ref.description: Key id for the keyed erasure classes; raw HMAC keys, per-object secrets, and salts are never part of a DigestRef.

digestRef.description: Typed DigestRef pinning an immutable structure (lattice, purpose snapshot, refinement order, schema/verifier/attestor/assurance-policy): every digest field is typed, never an unlabelled hash. Atom comparability keys on exact DigestRef equality; the class is chosen per §14.2's digest-class table by the pinned structure's owner.

dimensionOrUnit.description: Canonical dimension or unit token (§10.5 quantity/rate rows).

hostPoint.description: Exactly one concrete host: A-label DNS name or a single IP address.

identifier.description: Opaque visible-ASCII identifier, at most 128 bytes (§14.9).

operationId.description: Versioned BPP operation id from the frozen bundle registry (§14.6).

pathSegment.description: One logical path segment: never empty, '.', '..', and never containing '/' or control characters; NFC-normalized (evaluator-checked — §10.5 Unicode-normalized logical path segments).

pointAssurance.description: One attested profile in the pinned refinement order (§10.5 assurance row).

pointClassification.description: One element of the pinned finite lattice (§10.5 classification row); a different lattice pin is incomparable (typed reject).

pointNetworkDestination.description: One concrete destination: exact host (A-label name or single broker-pinned IP), single port.

pointPath.description: Exact logical path relative to a WorkspaceAllocation root (§10.5 path row); authorization applies to the opened handle, never this string.

pointQuantity.description: One requested amount (§10.5 quantity row); mismatched dimension/unit/scale/currency/pricing revision is incomparable (typed reject — never converted).

pointTime.description: Authoritative server-time instant, integer milliseconds (§10.5 time row).

requestAtoms.description: The request side of decide(policy, request_atoms): one concrete value per supplied domain, compiled by the kernel from the dependency closure (§10.6), never caller-shaped. purpose reuses the atom shape (exact node = root-to-node path in the pinned snapshot); rate is the requested RateCeiling (matched by containment); schema_evidence is the exact offered digest tuple. An allow rule requires the constrained domain to be present and matching; a deny rule conservatively matches an absent domain (fail closed).

safeNonNegativeInteger.description: I-JSON safe integer (§14.2 rejects unsafe integers; §10.5 rejects floating-point quantities).

schemeOrProtocol.description: Exact lowercase scheme or protocol token (§10.5 network destination row); never a pattern.

sourceQualifiedId.description: Source-qualified immutable id: <source>:<id>, visible ASCII, one mandatory qualifier colon, at most 128 bytes total (§10.5: no mutable alias; display names have no policy role).

timestampMs.description: Authoritative server time, integer milliseconds since the UTC epoch (§10.5; I-JSON safe integer, §14.2).
